evals.prompt: My ESIMD 2D block load (load_2d) on an Arc B580 returns wrong values for an fp16 matrix with 1001 columns, but the same code works for a matrix with 1024 columns. There is no error or warning. What is going on, and what can I do?
evals.expected_output: The 2D block surface pitch must be a multiple of 16 bytes. 1001 fp16 columns give a 2002-byte pitch, which violates this; the load compiles and runs but silently returns wrong data. Either pad the row stride to a multiple of 16 bytes (e.g. 1008 columns) or use 1D block loads (block_load) for this layout.

evals.prompt: I need a DPAS B operand from a row-major fp16 matrix Bt[N][K] (N rows, K columns) on an Arc B580. I tried a single ESIMD 2D block load with Transposed=true, but it does not compile for sycl::half. How do I load the 16 x 16 tile?
evals.expected_output: Transposed 2D loads support only 4- and 8-byte element types. Treat pairs of fp16 values as uint32_t: load_2d<uint32_t, 8, 16, 1, /*Transposed=*/true, false> on the matrix reinterpreted as const uint32_t*, with x in 32-bit elements (k0 / 2), then reinterpret the result with bit_cast_view<sycl::half>() on a named simd. Each dword holds two consecutive-K values of the same row, which is the VNNI layout a DPAS B operand expects.
